title: Map a two-wire harness with two flying probes and record its verdict
instruction: 1. Verify the isolated two-wire harness. On the upright panel, A is lower left and B upper left; C lower right and D upper right. Pick up the orange and blue probes. 2. Measure AC, AD, BC and BD. Hold both spring tips on the named pads for at least 0.5 s. The meter shows 1 for a connected 1-ohm path, OL for no path, and -- when a tip is disconnected. OL counts only while both tips visibly contact the pads. Withdraw before changing pairs. 3. Write the four results in AC,AD,BC,BD order, using 1 for continuity and 0 for OL: 1001 means PASS, 0110 means CROSSED, 1000 or 0001 means OPEN. Any other pattern needs rechecking. 4. Return both probes flat to their starting places. Move the blue result tag onto P for PASS, X for CROSSED or O for OPEN. Release it, open both grippers and withdraw. Leave the probes and tag still for two seconds.
context: Verify an isolated two-conductor harness by measuring all four inter-end connections, interpreting a pin-map table, and recording PASS, CROSSED or OPEN with a physical result tag. The measurement needs simultaneous contact by two free spring-tip probes.
setup: Station YAM arms, original rigid test fixture. Coordinates in cm: x forward, y left from the arm-base midpoint; heights above table. Four flush 2.6 cm square pads on an upright 29x20 cm panel at x=36: A/B at y=9 and heights10/15; C/D at y=-9 and heights10/15. Covered wiring is a declared isolated two-wire graph; default A-D and B-C (crossed). Alternatives A-C+B-D, A-C only or B-D only. Two loose probe handles, 4.5x2.5x4.6 cm and90g, start at(19,+/-15), height2.3. Each15g metal tip extends6.5 cm forward from its handle origin; native axial guide permits8mm compression with200N/m spring,1mm preload and1Ns/m damping. The meter has a16x22cm white face centred(46,33.5), height12, with large black --, OL or1. Probe lead dynamics are omitted. A blue2.5x2.5x3.6cm,50g result tag starts(16,0). Marked8cm square result areas P/X/O are centred(14,22),(24,22),(34,22), with4mm-thick bases. Fixed layout; no randomization. Intended construction materials: polymer probe handles and result tag, metal tips/contact pads and guide springs, insulating polymer panel/result-area bases and meter housing/face. Simulation uses the authored rigid-body masses and friction.
scoring: 0.15 for each distinct AC,AD,BC,BD measurement held continuously0.5s with both contacts valid (maximum0.6). Each tip needs1-8.5mm measured spring compression, guide lateral error<1mm, axis within10deg of panel normal, distal face within2mm of pad plane and centre within11mm of pad centre. OL without both contacts earns nothing. 0.2 more for the correct tag position from the four measured bits (1001=P,0110=X,1000/0001=O), tag centre within25mm in x/y, height22+/-4mm and upright within15deg. Full1.0 requires both probes within3cm of starting x/y, centre height23+/-4mm and upright within15deg, all free bodies slower than2cm/s, both grippers>80% open and TCPs>7cm from handles/tag for2s. Invalid numeric state invalidates that step and resets settling/hold. Start scores0.
reset_notes: Return probes to their starting poses, restore each spring tip to its uncompressed stop, return the result tag to(16,0), clear measurement history and show --. Default wiring remains crossed; wiring alternatives are explicit embodiment options.
fidelity: Native contacts compress passive spring tips against flush pads. Compression and tip/pad alignment validate contact independently of continuity; an explicit wire graph yields nominal1-ohm or OL readings. PhysX does not simulate electricity. Lead dynamics and internal guide collisions are omitted. Kinematic glyphs reproduce the meter display only. Fixture dimensions and friction are nominal original training hardware.
scores: Dream-1:0.0 (one trial,1100 actions/55 s); scripted demo:1.0; reset repeat:1.0 (40.6 s each).
